answer: Reputation Decay Pricing. Each new identity starts at a low trust score, so its transactions carry a high fee multiplier that falls only as consistent history accumulates. A gale of fresh accounts thus pays steep premiums on every action with no way to skip the climb. The fee curve follows a downward spiral as genuine activity builds, while a mass of new identities stays pinned at the costly top. Verifying one costs an opal-tier deposit plus sustained fees, so each fake identity is a recurring drain, not a one-time gate.
